title: Hamiltonian curl-forces in systems coupled to multiple thermal reservoirs
authors: Omer Chor, Aljaž Godec, Oren Raz
abstract: We investigate the statistical mechanics of a system coupled to multiple heat reservoirs at different temperatures, a setting which typically sustains nontrivial circulation. By applying a canonical transformation, we map the system onto that of a particle coupled to a single reservoir yet driven by a deterministic curl-force---a reversible, velocity-independent non-conservative force with non-vanishing curl---that can be described by a Hamiltonian with an anisotropic kinetic energy term. Despite the Hamiltonian structure, the system does not relax to the corresponding Boltzmann distribution, and is genuinely out of equilibrium. The mapping provides a mechanical interpretation of the currents in multi-temperature systems, as we demonstrate by means of two examples. In particular, the direction of circulation is qualitatively predictable from the deterministic force field. For the exactly solvable case of an $N$-dimensional underdamped Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, we derive explicit expressions for the steady-state distribution and the entropy production rate, highlighting the role of the (generalized) curl of the force field in driving the system out of thermal equilibrium. Finally, we show how a non-conservative force can be used to exactly equilibrate any system coupled to multiple reservoirs, and obtain the corresponding equilibrium distribution.
summary: This paper analyzes the statistical mechanics of systems coupled to multiple heat baths at different temperatures, showing that this coupling generates non-equilibrium steady states. The authors map this complex system onto an effective single-bath description driven by a deterministic curl-force. This framework provides a mechanical understanding of non-equilibrium currents and quantifies the system's departure from equilibrium via the entropy production rate.
main_problem: Investigating the statistical mechanics of systems coupled to multiple heat reservoirs at different temperatures, a setting that typically sustains non-trivial circulation and drives the system out of equilibrium.
main_result: The multi-reservoir dynamics can be mapped onto an effective single-bath system driven by a deterministic curl-force, leading to non-equilibrium steady states (NESS) characterized by non-zero entropy production.
method: The authors employ a canonical transformation to map the complex multi-reservoir coupling onto a simpler, effective Hamiltonian structure featuring an anisotropic kinetic energy and a curl-force.
model_or_system: The model is a classical open system (e.g., underdamped Brownian particle) whose dynamics are governed by a generalized Klein-Kramers equation describing coupling to multiple baths at different temperatures ($T_i$).

important_parameters: Multiple reservoir temperatures ($T_i$), damping coefficient ($\xi$), and the mass ($m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system dynamics and assumes the validity of the canonical transformation, though the resulting steady state is generally not the simple Boltzmann distribution.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the non-equilibrium nature of multi-reservoir coupling, then applies a canonical transformation to derive an effective single-bath description driven by a curl-force. Finally, explicit derivations for the steady-state distribution and EPR are provided for solvable cases.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful mechanical interpretation of non-equilibrium thermodynamics, showing how multi-temperature baths manifest as deterministic, non-conservative forces, which is highly relevant for understanding energy flow in open quantum systems.
